concept.name: Under-collateralized loan
concept.definition: An under-collateralized loan is a loan where the borrower's collateral is worth less than the outstanding debt — either by design (credit-based or flash loans) or by deterioration (a liquidated-too-late position that becomes protocol bad debt).
concept.intuition: It is lending on trust rather than on locked value — normal in banking, but the exception in DeFi, where code cannot chase a borrower for the difference.
concept.mechanics: Mainstream DeFi lending is overcollateralized, so under-collateralized lending appears only in special forms: flash loans (zero collateral, repaid atomically in the same transaction), credit delegation (a depositor delegates borrowing power to a trusted party), and undercollateralized institutional credit pools with legal agreements. When a normal position becomes undercollateralized faster than liquidators act, the deficit becomes bad debt socialized across the protocol.
concept.failure_modes: Without excess collateral, default risk returns: credit delegation and institutional pools depend on legal enforcement or reputation rather than code, and defaults cannot be clawed back trustlessly; bad debt from failed liquidations is absorbed by the protocol's suppliers.
concept.misconceptions: Under-collateralized does not mean unsecured-in-the-moment for flash loans — atomicity is a stronger guarantee than collateral. Conversely, an 'overcollateralized' loan is only as safe as its collateral's liquidity and oracle, and can silently become undercollateralized in a crash.
concept.example: A flash loan of 50,000 ETH is 'undercollateralized' for ~12 seconds yet riskless to Aave because repayment is enforced in the same transaction; by contrast, a $1M institutional credit line with $600k collateral relies on contracts and courts if the borrower defaults.
